Below is a quick‑reference table that shows which dog breeds kept a spot in the **top 10** of the American Kennel Club’s (AKC) “Most Popular Dog Breeds” lists for every year from **2013 through 2024**.

> **A breed that appears in the top‑10 for *every* single year (2013‑2024) is called “consistently top‑10.”  
>  The table lists each breed that was consistently top‑10, along with the year‑by‑year ranking for that dog.  
>  (Some years skip a ranking because the breed fell out of the top‑10; the “-” indicates “not in the top‑10 that year.”)

| 6 | **French Bulldog** | ‑ | 6 | 6 | 6 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| 7 | **Yorkshire Terrier** | 6 | 7 | 7 | 7 | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 |
| 8 | **Poodle** | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 7 | 8 | 7 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 |
| 9 | **Boxer** | 7 | 9 | 10 | 10 | 11 | 11 | 11 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 |
| 10 | **Rottweiler** | 9 | ‑ | 9 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 |

### Key take‑aways

| Breeds that were **consistently in the top‑10 every single year** 2013‑2024 | Notes |
|-------------------------------------------|-------|
| **Labrador Retriever** | Dominant in every list (rank 1). |
| **German Shepherd Dog** | Always rank 2. |
| **Golden Retriever** | Always rank 3. |
| **Bulldog** | Top‑10 every year (sometimes Rank 4, sometimes Rank 5). |
| **Beagle** | Top‑10 every year. |
| **French Bulldog** | Top‑10 only after 2014 but remained every year thereafter (rank 4–6). |
| **Yorkshire Terrier** | Top‑10 since 2013 (nth‑place fluctuated 6th–12th). |
| **Poodle** | Top‑10 every year with ranks mostly 6th–8th. |
| **Boxer** | Top‑10 each year, though often near the bottom of the list. |
| **Rottweiler** | Appeared in the top‑10 from 2013 through 2019, and again after 2019 (rank 8). |

> **Breeds that *broke* the streak**  
> * Dachshund – top‑10 only in 2013.  
> * Others (e.g., French Bulldog, Yorkshire Terrier) entered the top‑10 in later years but were **not** present in 2013.

## Privacy Preference Center

When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to find out more and change our default settings. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.   
[AKC Privacy Notice](https://www.akc.org/privacy/)
